articles.title: Nvidia’s biggest RAM supplier just had a trillion-dollar debut on Wall Street
articles.summary: SK Hynix has made a record-breaking debut on the US stock market. The South Korean chipmaker opened at $170 and raised $26.5 billion, making it the largest debut of a foreign company since Alibaba.
articles.body: As the AI boom boosts demand for RAM, SK Hynix — one of the world’s biggest suppliers of memory chips — launched on Wall Street Friday. The South Korean chipmaker opened at $170 per share and raised $26.5 billion, surpassing Alibaba’s record as the largest debut of a foreign company, according to reports from The Associated Press and CNN. After reaching a $1 trillion valuation in May, SK Hynix briefly overtook Samsung as South Korea’s most valuable company. SK Hynix is one of three major companies benefitting from a surge in demand for DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM). These components have become essential for the widespread buildout of AI data centers, as tech giants like OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google use DRAM for the servers to power their AI models, while HBM comes packaged inside high-end AI chips like Nvidia’s Blackwell Ultra. As of June 2026, SK Hynix makes up 29 percent of the global DRAM market, with Samsung at 38 percent and Micron at 22 percent, according to data from Counterpoint. The three giants still can’t keep up with memory demand as they continue to prioritize high-paying AI customers over device makers who need the chips for phones, computers, consoles, and more. SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won said in June that the company plans to ramp up its memory chip capacity over the next five years to address a shortage that could last until 2030, Bloomberg reports.

articles.title: Endividamento de risco cresce 75% em 5 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Relatório do Banco Central mostra que pessoas que ganham até dois salários mínimos têm 42% da renda comprometida com dívidas.
articles.summary: Relatório do Banco Central mostra que pessoas que ganham até dois salários mínimos têm 42% da renda comprometida com dívidas.
articles.body:
Cerca de 20,3 milhões de brasileiros estavam em situação de endividamento de risco em junho de 2026 , o equivalente a 17% das pessoas que têm dívidas no Sistema Financeiro Nacional (SFN).

O número representa um crescimento de 75% em cinco anos, segundo relatório de Estabilidade Financeira do Banco Central (BC) divulgado na terça-feira (27).

🔍Comprar um produto parcelado, financiar um imóvel ou pagar uma compra no cartão de crédito são exemplos de situações que geram dívidas, onde entra a classificação de endividado. Isso não significa, por si só, que a pessoa esteja com pagamentos atrasados ou tenha dificuldades financeiras, aí entraria a inadimplência.

Para classificar alguém como endividado de risco, o BC considera a combinação de pelo menos dois de quatro critérios, que incluem:

Comprometimento de mais da metade da renda mensal com dívidas.

Renda restante abaixo da linha da pobreza após o pagamento dos débitos.

Uso simultâneo de cheque especial, crédito pessoal sem consignação e crédito rotativo.

Endividamento de risco segundo o BC — Foto: g1

Famílias mais pobres comprometem maior parte da renda com dívidas

➡️ O peso das dívidas no orçamento é maior entre os brasileiros de baixa renda . Para quem ganha até dois salários mínimos, o pagamento das dívidas compromete 42% da renda mensal. Desse total, 15% da renda é destinada ao pagamento de dívidas do cartão de crédito.

Essa faixa reúne 61,2 milhões de tomadores de crédito no Sistema Financeiro Nacional (SFN) e concentra um perfil de endividamento mais associado a modalidades de crédito de alto custo, como cartão de crédito e empréstimos pessoais sem consignação.

Segundo o relatório do Banco Central (BC), a participação dessas modalidades cresceu de forma mais intensa entre os consumidores de menor renda.

Já entre as pessoas que ganham mais de dez salários mínimos, o comprometimento da renda com dívidas é de 18,6%.

Nesse grupo, que reúne 4,4 milhões de tomadores de crédito, uma parcela maior dos pagamentos está associada a financiamentos imobiliários e de veículos, geralmente ligados à aquisição de bens e com prazos mais longos.

O relatório também identifica outros dois grupos de renda: 22,3 milhões de tomadores ganham entre dois e cinco salários mínimos, enquanto 7,5 milhões recebem entre cinco e dez salários mínimos.

Endividamento de risco cresce desde 2021

Em junho de 2021, 9,7% dos tomadores de crédito estavam em situação de endividamento de risco. A proporção subiu para 13,1% em junho de 2022 e chegou a 13,8% em junho de 2023. Depois de recuar para 13,4% em junho de 2024, voltou a subir e alcançou 17% em junho de 2026.

Banco Central vê riscos na oferta de crédito digital

O relatório aponta que a oferta frequente de crédito em canais digitais pode estimular a contratação de empréstimos sem planejamento , especialmente entre consumidores de menor renda.

➡️ Segundo pesquisa citada pelo BC, esse público recebe, em média, nove ofertas digitais de crédito por mês.

A instituição também estuda medidas para reduzir riscos associados à concessão de crédito e à forma como os produtos são oferecidos.

O relatório também aponta problemas na modalidade Crédito do Trabalhador, criada para oferecer empréstimos consignados a trabalhadores do setor privado.

Em junho de 2026, o saldo de operações inadimplentes nessa linha chegou a R$ 6,1 bilhões.

Segundo o BC, parte desse valor estava associada a trabalhadores que perderam o emprego, enquanto outra parcela correspondia a pessoas que foram demitidas e conseguiram uma nova colocação formal.

articles.title: Emissão online da CIPTEA facilita rotina de pessoas autistas em Macaé | G1
articles.standfirst: Carteira pode ser solicitada pela internet, com acompanhamento do pedido e acesso à versão digital. O serviço é gratuito.
articles.summary: Carteira pode ser solicitada pela internet, com acompanhamento do pedido e acesso à versão digital. O serviço é gratuito.
articles.body:
Sistema online otimiza e centraliza todas as etapas do pedido do documento — Foto: Arquivo Secom

A Prefeitura de Macaé disponibiliza uma plataforma online para a emissão da Carteira de Identificação da Pessoa com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (CIPTEA). O serviço é gratuito e visa otimizar o tempo das famílias de pessoas autistas, permitindo solicitar o documento, acompanhar a análise do pedido e acessar a versão digital pelo celular ou computador, sem a necessidade de comparecimento presencial para dar entrada no processo.

Com a implantação da ferramenta, o procedimento anterior — que permitia o envio de solicitações pelo antigo e-mail institucional — foi totalmente encerrado. A mudança tem como objetivo tornar o atendimento mais organizado, seguro e eficiente, centralizando todas as etapas em um único ambiente digital. O sistema foi desenvolvido pela Secretaria Municipal de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação, em parceria com a Secretaria Municipal de Desenvolvimento Social, Direitos Humanos, Acessibilidade e Economia Solidária (SEMDES).

A plataforma conta com mecanismos rigorosos de proteção de dados sensíveis, passando por auditorias constantes e testes nas ferramentas para evitar qualquer risco de vazamento de informações, mantendo o acesso estritamente restrito. A iniciativa representa uma modernização dos serviços públicos e uma facilidade para os usuários, que acompanham a liberação da solicitação à distância, reforçando a acessibilidade, a inclusão e a proteção social no município.

Para os familiares e responsáveis por pessoas autistas, a facilidade de realizar o processo pela internet proporciona um ganho expressivo de tempo no dia a dia. A possibilidade de efetuar o cadastro e o envio de documentos do próprio celular ou computador ajuda quem não tem com quem deixar a criança, permitindo fazer a solicitação de casa, do trabalho ou até mesmo na sala de espera de atendimentos de saúde e terapias.

A CIPTEA possui validade em todo o território nacional e ajuda a garantir direitos previstos em lei, como o atendimento prioritário. Em Macaé, a carteira foi instituída pelo Decreto Municipal nº 007/2020, em conformidade com a Lei Federal nº 13.977/2020 (Lei Romeo Mion).

Para solicitar o documento, o cidadão deve acessar o portal ciptea.macae.rj.gov.br, preencher os dados solicitados, anexar a documentação exigida acompanhada de uma foto recente e acompanhar a análise do pedido diretamente pelo site. Após a aprovação, a versão digital pode ser baixada. Para aqueles que preferirem obter a carteira física, é possível solicitar a opção na própria plataforma e seguir as orientações disponíveis para a retirada presencial do documento impresso.

articles.title: Diesel mais caro pressiona o agro e o frete; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida mantém benefício de R$ 2,12 por litro em meio à alta do petróleo. Dependência de importações e transporte rodoviário ampliam os efeitos do diesel caro sobre fretes, produção e preços dos alimentos.
articles.summary: Medida mantém benefício de R$ 2,12 por litro em meio à alta do petróleo. Dependência de importações e transporte rodoviário ampliam os efeitos do diesel caro sobre fretes, produção e preços dos alimentos.
articles.body:
O governo federal prorrogou nesta terça-feira (27), por mais 30 dias, o subsídio ao diesel, mantendo o benefício em R$ 2,12 por litro. A medida busca conter os efeitos da alta dos preços internacionais do petróleo , principal matéria-prima do combustível, pressionados pelos conflitos no Oriente Médio e pela guerra entre Rússia e Ucrânia.

O barril do petróleo Brent, referência internacional, foi negociado entre US$ 100 e US$ 106 na primeira quinzena de outubro e chegou a US$ 113,17 no dia 22. Para o governo, qualquer valor acima dos US$ 70 gera pressão forte nos preços para o mercado interno.

Além da alta da commodity, a desvalorização do real também pode encarecer a produção e a importação de diesel. Apesar de ser um grande produtor de petróleo, o Brasil importa cerca de um quinto do diesel que consome, segundo dados da Agência Nacional do Petróleo (ANP).

Em agosto, o diesel importado correspondeu a 23,14% das vendas nacionais de diesel A, combustível ainda sem a mistura obrigatória de biodiesel.

A junção desses fatores dá no seguinte resultado:

O preço do diesel comum subiu 6,67% na primeira quinzena de outubro , chegando à média de R$ 7,20 por litro, segundo o Índice de Preços Edenred Ticket Log (IPTL). Já o diesel S-10 ficou 5,07% mais caro no período, chegando a R$ 7,46 por litro. Em relação a janeiro, o diesel comum acumulou aumento de 15,2%.

Os preços também variam entre as regiões do país. No Norte, o litro do diesel comum custava, em média, R$ 7,75, enquanto o S-10 tinha preço médio de R$ 7,80. Em Roraima, o diesel comum chegou a R$ 8,19; no Acre, o S-10 atingiu R$ 8,30. No Sul e no Sudeste, a média do diesel comum era de R$ 6,97 por litro.

Esse aumento que se reflete no transporte de cargas, feito principalmente por caminhões no Brasil. No agronegócio, o combustível mais caro eleva o custo do frete e da produção, e esse aumento pode ser repassado aos preços dos alimentos.

Como mostrou o Globo Rural , agricultores do Rio Grande do Sul já demonstram preocupação com a possível falta de diesel às vésperas do plantio da safra de verão.

Por que o Brasil precisa importar diesel?

Entre janeiro e agosto, a produção de diesel pela Petrobras chegou a crescer 18,5%, passando de 32,7 milhões para 38,7 milhões de barris. Ainda assim, a produção nacional não foi suficiente para atender a toda a demanda pelo combustível.

No primeiro semestre de 2026, o Brasil consumiu 213,2 milhões de barris de diesel. Segundo a ANP, a produção nacional foi de 154,8 milhões de barris , enquanto as importações somaram 43,5 milhões de barris , o equivalente a 20,4% do consumo no período.

A dependência de importações está relacionada à capacidade de refino do país. Isso porque extrair petróleo não é o mesmo que produzir combustíveis: o petróleo precisa ser processado em refinarias para se transformar em diesel e outros derivados usados por caminhões, máquinas agrícolas e veículos.

Nos últimos anos, a Petrobras vendeu refinarias para empresas privadas como parte de um programa de venda de ativos. Esse movimento ganhou força durante o governo de Jair Bolsonaro (PL), quando a estatal negociou unidades do setor de refino.

O professor Paulo Feldmann, da Faculdade de Economia, Administração, Contabilidade e Atuária da Universidade de São Paulo (FEA-USP), questiona os custos de produção do diesel nessas refinarias e afirma que, em algumas situações, o combustível produzido no Brasil chega a ser mais caro que o importado.

Já Francismar Ferreira, do Instituto de Estudos Estratégicos de Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (Ineep), afirma que diminuir a dependência das importações exige ampliar e modernizar as refinarias brasileiras, além de rever os investimentos da Petrobras no setor.

Por que a alta do diesel pesa tanto no Brasil?

🕰️ A partir da segunda metade do século XX, o Brasil passou a priorizar o transporte de cargas por rodovias, enquanto as ferrovias perderam espaço. Essa mudança acompanhou o crescimento da indústria automobilística e a expansão da malha rodoviária.

Hoje, a dependência das estradas faz com que a alta do diesel aumente os custos do frete e, consequentemente, do transporte de mercadorias.

“Os combustíveis em geral, sobretudo gasolina e diesel, têm um impacto muito grande sobre o transporte de mercadorias. O Brasil é um país grande e precisa transportar cargas por longas distâncias, isso afeta muito a produtividade do Brasil”, afirma Paulo Feldmann, da FEA-USP.

➡️ Países como Argentina e Estados Unidos também sofrem com a alta dos combustíveis, mas contam com redes ferroviárias que permitem escoar parte da produção agrícola e industrial por trens, diminuindo a dependência das rodovias em determinados trajetos.

Há também riscos para o abastecimento, como alertam os agricultores do RS. Murilo Viana, mestre em economia pela Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp), avalia que os subsídios concedidos recentemente pelo governo, ao manter os preços internos artificialmente abaixo dos internacionais, podem desestimular empresas privadas a importar diesel.

Nesse cenário, a Petrobras poderia ser pressionada a assumir uma parcela maior das importações, eventualmente vendendo o combustível com prejuízo por litro. Caso isso não ocorra, o país poderia enfrentar dificuldades de abastecimento por falta de importação pela iniciativa privada.

Como isso afeta os preços dos alimentos?

O agronegócio está entre os setores mais afetados pela alta do diesel, já que o combustível é utilizado tanto nas máquinas agrícolas, durante o preparo do solo, o plantio e a colheita, quanto no transporte da produção até armazéns, indústrias, portos e centros consumidores.

“O aumento dos custos pode reduzir a competitividade das exportações e encarecer os alimentos no mercado interno”, afirma Paulo Feldmann, da FEA-USP.

“Todos falam que 'da porteira para dentro' a agricultura brasileira é a mais competitiva do mundo. O Brasil perde muito no transporte, que é o que mais afeta o custo.”

Com o frete mais caro, produtores e empresas podem ter seus lucros reduzidos ou repassar parte dos custos adicionais aos compradores.

O repasse, porém, não acontece necessariamente de forma integral ou imediata. Parte do aumento pode ser absorvida ao longo da cadeia de produção e distribuição, dependendo dos contratos, da concorrência e das margens de lucro das empresas.

Nesse contexto, o governo Lula tem apostado em subsídios temporários para conter os efeitos de altas de preços que considera passageiras.

A prorrogação do subsídio anunciada pelo governo busca reduzir os efeitos da alta dos preços internacionais do petróleo no Brasil. Para Feldmann, a medida pode ajudar a conter o repasse dos custos, mas tem limites porque depende de recursos públicos, em um momento de dificuldades nas contas do governo.

Para Murilo Viana, o subsídio pode ser justificado pelo fato de que a alta dos preços internacionais do petróleo também pode elevar a arrecadação do governo brasileiro . Isso porque o país exporta petróleo bruto e recebe receitas de royalties, dividendos da Petrobras e tributos.

O subsídio, portanto, representa um gasto imediato para o governo, mas pode ajudar a evitar custos e impactos maiores sobre a economia. O resultado dessa estratégia, porém, depende de quanto o governo arrecada a mais com o petróleo, de quanto gasta com o subsídio e de quanto do aumento do diesel chegaria aos preços de outros produtos.

Para Viana, medidas para estabilizar os preços podem ser válidas, desde que sejam temporárias e tenham regras claras para seu encerramento , evitando que o subsídio se transforme em uma forma permanente de manter os preços artificialmente baixos.

O que reduziria a dependência brasileira?

Ampliar a capacidade de refino, investir em alternativas de transporte e reduzir a dependência de insumos importados são medidas que podem, na visão dos analistas, tornar o Brasil menos vulnerável.

Para Francismar Ferreira, do Ineep, uma solução de longo prazo exige ampliar e modernizar as refinarias brasileiras, além de aumentar os investimentos no setor.

A discussão também envolve o papel da Petrobras na produção de combustíveis derivados do petróleo, assim como na distribuição e revenda desses produtos.

O economista Murilo Viana também defende ampliar a produção nacional de fertilizantes, outro insumo essencial para o agronegócio.

Essa medida não resolve diretamente a dependência do diesel, mas faz parte de uma estratégia mais ampla para reduzir a vulnerabilidade do setor às oscilações do dólar e dos insumos no mercado internacional.

articles.title: Empréstimo dos Correios: Governo garante R$ 7 bi após as eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Novo empréstimo já havia sido confirmado pelos Correios nas demonstrações financeiras do 1º semestre deste ano, divulgadas no final de agosto. Aporte era esperado para setembro, mas saiu apenas após o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais.
articles.summary: Com garantia do governo, o empréstimo dos Correios de R$ 7 bilhões visa a reestruturação da estatal, que acumula 15 trimestres seguidos de prejuízo financeiro.
articles.body:
O governo federal concedeu garantia de R$ 7 bilhões para empréstimo de um consórcio de bancos aos Correios , dentro do processo de reestruturação previsto para o período de 2025 a 2027.

O ato foi formalizado após a conclusão do segundo turno das eleições presidenciais, realizado neste domingo (25), que terminou com a vitória do candidato petista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva .

A medida consta em despacho do ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, publicado no Diário Oficial da União.

O consórcio de bancos, formado por pelo ABC Brasil, Citibank, Deutsche Bank e pelo JP Morgan, com isso, tem a garantia de que vai receber as parcelas do empréstimo do Tesouro Nacional — no caso de os Correios não honrarem o compromisso.

O novo empréstimo, no valor de R$ 7 bilhões, já havia sido confirmado pelos Correios nas demonstrações financeiras do 1º semestre deste ano, divulgadas no final de agosto.

Em setembro, os Correios informaram ao g1 que o empréstimo saísse ainda naquele mês , algo que não aconteceu, sendo formalizado apenas após o segundo turno da eleições para presidente da República.

Na ocasião, a estatal também confirmou o compromisso firmado com o governo federal para o aporte de R$ 6 bilhões na empresa até o final de 2027.

Os Correios estão há 15 trimestres seguidos no vermelho. No primeiro semestre deste ano, a empresa fechou com um prejuízo de R$ 5,6 bilhões.

O prejuízo do 2º trimestre é menor do que o obtido pela empresa nos últimos dois trimestres, o 1º deste ano e o 4º trimestre de 2025, apontando um pequeno movimento de recuperação da saúde financeira dos Correios, que teve um prejuízo recorde no 1º trimestre de 2026.

O resultado dos Correios tem contribuído para o rombo das estatais federais, que somou R$ 6,51 bilhões nos oito primeiros meses deste ano , segundo dados do Banco Central. O resultado, que é recorde na parcial deste ano, fica próximo do maior rombo já contabilizado para um ano fechado (-R$ 6,73 bilhões em 2024).

Para enfrentar rombo financeiro, o governo autorizou, em maio deste ano, a estatal a vender seguros, títulos de capitalização e a atuar no mercado de telefonia. A ideia é que a empresa faça convênios com instituições financeiras para ofertar os serviços. De acordo com o Ministério da Gestão, os Correios executam um plano de reequilíbrio financeiro e reestruturação.

articles.title: Vídeo de 2025 não mostra plano de Lula para acabar com Bolsa Família | G1
articles.standfirst: Posts enganosos reproduzem conteúdo veiculado pela CNN no ano passado e tiram material de contexto. Ao Fato ou Fake, Ministério do Desenvolvimento desmentiu alegações.
articles.summary: Posts enganosos usam reportagem da CNN sobre regra de transição e mentem ao citar encerramento do programa. Ao Fato ou Fake, Ministério do Desenvolvimento desmentiu alegações.
articles.body:
É #FAKE que reportagem citou plano de Lula para acabar com Bolsa Família após 2º turno; vídeo de 2025 relatou mudanças no programa — Foto: Reprodução

Circulam nas redes sociais publicações com um vídeo de uma reportagem supostamente relatando que, após a vitória no segundo turno das eleições , o governo do presidente Lula ( PT ) acabaria com o Bolsa Família. É #FAKE .

Compartilhadas no Instagram , Facebook e X desde segunda-feira (26), as publicações têm esta caixa de texto sobreposta às imagens: "Bolsa Família pode acabar! Bolsa Família pode estar com os dias contados. Governo Lula avalia a possibilidade de encerrar o programa" .

Veja dois exemplos de legendas: "Depois de ganhar as eleições Lula vai acabar com o bolsa família. Faz o L" ; e "Governo Lula avalia a possibilidade de encerrar o programa".

Mas esses posts são mentirosos. Embora seja real – e não um conteúdo fabricado por inteligência artificial (IA) –, o vídeo compartilhado não mostra uma reportagem sobre o fim do Bolsa Família. Trata-se, na verdade, de um conteúdo jornalístico exibido em 16 abril de 2025 pela CNN, no qual os jornalistas Marcio Gomes e Jussara Soares comentam regras para beneficiários saírem do programa. Intitulado "Análise: Governo quer emplacar ideia de transição ao Bolsa Família", o material não cita qualquer medida para acabar com a iniciativa (leia mais abaixo) .

No vídeo, a jornalista comenta sobre uma nova "regra de transição" apresentada pelo governo federal no ano passado , que alterou o tempo de permanência no programa das famílias que ultrapassem o limite de renda.

O Bolsa Família é um programa de assistência social destinado para cidadãos com renda familiar per capita de até R$ 218 .

Anteriormente, se a renda per capita chegasse ao máximo de R$ 759, a família continuaria recebendo metade do valor do benefício ao longo do prazo de até dois anos.

Com as mudanças, implantadas a partir de junho de 2025, o prazo diminuiu para um ano para os novos beneficiários. E o valor limite ficou em R$ 706.

Famílias que ultrapassam o limite continuaram saindo do programa imediatamente.

Procurada pelo Fato ou Fake , a assessoria de imprensa do Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS), responsável pelo programa, afirmou que "são falsas as alegações de cortes no Bolsa Família" que passaram a circular recentemente.

Em nota enviada por e-mail, a pasta informou: "O programa segue em funcionamento, sem suspensão de pagamentos ou redução dos benefícios. Em outubro, houve reajuste de 15,04%, com o valor mínimo por família passando de R$ 600 para R$ 691" .

Esse reajuste foi anunciado pelo governo Lula em 17 de setembro , a 17 dias do primeiro turno da eleição. O primeiro repasse com valores atualizados ocorreu em 19 de outubro , sete dias antes do segundo turno das eleições , que terminou com o presidente reeleito para seu quarto mandato, após vitória sobre Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ).

À época do anúncio do aumento para o Bolsa Família, o governo negou motivação eleitoral e afirmou que a medida recompõe parte da perda do poder de compra causada pela inflação desde o aumento anterior, três anos atrás. De acordo com dados do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), o Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC) acumulado entre março de 2023 e agosto de 2026 foi de 15,04%.

Economistas e especialistas consultados pelo g1 questionaram o momento da alteração e o risco às contas públicas .

articles.title: India open to free, fair trade with China: Piyush Goyal

articles.body: HAGUE: India is open to promoting free and fair trade with China and hopes to expand its exports of goods and services to the neighbouring country and Asean region in the coming years, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said late Monday, signalling scope for deeper trade engagement with Beijing.Goyal told reporters that India believed in open trade across the world and was looking for open markets in different countries on a reciprocal basis to sell Indian goods and services. “Yes, at some stage maybe we will do that also,” he said when asked if India was considering a similar exercise with China after concluding talks on a trade agreement with the European Union (EU).The minister said he had met his Chinese counterpart in Yaoundé, Cameroon, earlier this year and again in New Delhi during the latter’s visit for the Brics summit in Sept. “We are open to working and encouraging free and fair trade with every country around the globe. We are looking to open markets in different countries on a reciprocal basis for our goods and services also,” he said.As China supplies India with a number of critical intermediate goods and important raw materials, Goyal said there was an established judicial process that could be followed if it was ever found that the pricing of a particular good was not proper. “We believe in the rules of fair play, we believe in the rules of open trade across the world. Markets are open across the world. We welcome suppliers to meet the growing needs of India,” the minister said.Asked about China’s recent export controls on tunnelling equipment, which could impact several infrastructure projects, Goyal said he had learnt about the move after leaving India and that govt would work on the issue.According to commerce department data, China became India’s largest trading partner in the first half of the current fiscal year, with bilateral trade between the two countries rising 10.5% to $91.8 billion, with the trade deficit also expanding.While India has recently implemented trade deals with the UK and New Zealand and the EU agreement is expected to open markets in 27 European countries, Goyal said talks with Chile were nearing conclusion and those with Canada were making good progress. Mexico is keen on an “early-harvest” arrangement while negotiations with the South African Customs Union have just begun. He said India was working towards securing preferential access to economies accounting for 76% of the estimated $115 trillion global GDP.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: Jio platform share price: Jio Platforms Limited stock jumps over 23% Shares of Reliance Industries-backed Jio Platforms made a blockbuster stock market debut, rising nearly 23% over the issue price of Rs 1,119 and making the company India's second most valuable firm by market capitalisation. The stock listed at Rs 1,358 on both the BSE and NSE, marking a gain of 21.36% over the issue price. It later touched a high of Rs 1,375 on the BSE, up 22.87%, while on the NSE it climbed 22.83% to Rs 1,374.50. Jio Platforms' market valuation stood at Rs 12,57,401.07 crore..Jio Platforms listing: Akash Ambani says IPO 'response surpassed our imagination' Akash Ambani, chairman of Reliance Jio Infocomm, said the response to the IPO had exceeded the company’s expectations. The offering received demand worth more than Rs 7.5 lakh crore and over 1.3 crore applications. “The response surpassed our imagination, breaking records in every investor category. We were fully subscribed for India's largest IPO within 95 minutes of launch, the fastest ever India has seen,” he said. Ambani described the listing as the beginning of a new phase for the company, rather than an endpoint, and underlined its responsibility towards shareholders..Reliance Jio debuts today: Jio Platforms’ market capitalisation hits Rs 12.5 lakh crore Jio Platforms made a strong stock market debut with shares were trading at Rs 1,357.45, up Rs 238.45, or 21.31%, from the issue price. The stock touched an early high of Rs 1,374 before trading at around Rs 1,357. At these levels, Jio Platforms’ market capitalisation stood at around Rs 12.5 lakh crore. Reliance Industries, which holds a 64.48% stake in Jio Platforms, was trading at Rs 1,197 per share around 9.59 am, up 0.07% from its previous close of Rs 1,196.20. Speaking at the listing ceremony, Akash Ambani, chairman of Reliance Jio Infocomm, said the IPO had received demand worth more than Rs 7.5 lakh crore, along with over 1.3 crore applications, exceeding expectations..Jio Platforms debuts with 21% premium .Jio Platforms Limited debuts: Jio Platforms registers stellar opening at Dalal Street Shares of Jio Platforms, the country’s largest-ever public offering, made their stock market debut, listing at Rs 1,359 on the BSE and NSE, a 21.36% premium over the IPO price of Rs 1,119 per share. The Rs 30,200-crore IPO attracted cumulative demand of more than Rs 7 lakh crore across the anchor and public book-building process. Investor appetite was evident from the outset, with the issue being fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening. The Rs 5,500-crore portion reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) was subscribed within the first 10 minutes..Jio Platforms listing: Jio Platforms makes strong debut, lists at 21% premium to issue price Jio Platforms Limited (JPL) made a strong stock market debut on the NSE and BSE, with premium of Rs 250, or 22.34%, over its issue price of Rs 1,119. The stock was 1369.00, up 11 points or 0.81% on both benchmarks..Reliance Jio IPO lists today: Jio Platforms to debut Dalal Street shortly Jio Platforms shares were indicated at Rs 1,358 in the pre-listing session, a premium of Rs 239, or 21.36%, over the issue price. The company’s $3.2 billion initial public offering was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening for bids on October 21, drawing strong investor demand for India’s biggest-ever share sale. The IPO also marked the first public offering from the Reliance group in two decades..Jai Shree Krishna…Let me begin with the one word that matters most today: gratitude. I am deeply grateful to the millions who believed in Jio and made this day possible. Thank you all from the bottom of my heart. Today, the bell at the stock exchange will ring for me like a temple bell. For me, business is a form of worship, and every worship ritual concludes with prasad. We offer this day at the feet of Lord Ganesha, Dwarkanath Ji, Shrinathji, Balaji, and the living goddess, Bharat Mata…Many years ago, a dream emerged from an ordinary home in Chorwad. It belonged to a young man who worked at a petrol pump in Aden, with neither money nor recognition. That young man was our revered Grandfather Dhirubhai Ambani. He showed us that an ordinary Indian can dream extraordinary dreams. .Jio IPO listing today: ‘Business is puja,’ Anant Ambani expresses gratitude at Jio Platforms listing Speaking at the listing ceremony of Jio Platforms Limited, Reliance Industries Executive Director Anant Ambani began by expressing gratitude to the millions who had believed in Jio and made the occasion possible. “Let me begin with the one word that matters the most today, gratitude, to the millions who believed in Jio and made this day possible. I express my heartfelt gratitude towards you all,” he said. Ambani added that the exchange bell held a special significance for him, likening its sound to a temple bell. “Today, the bell at the Exchange will ring for me as a temple bell because for me business is puja and every puja ends with prasad, and prasad is always shared,” he said..Reliance Jio IPO: Investors upbeat on Jio Platforms’ debut as they await for the biggest IPO As Jio Platforms Ltd makes its stock market debut, an investor said the excitement was palpable, describing it as the biggest IPO. “The stock got oversubscribed in a few minutes. I am sure that Jio will be at the forefront of the Indian success story driven by the youth of the country,” the investor said..NSE is proud to welcome Jio Platforms Limited. Jio Platforms Limited becomes the 12th company from Reliance Industries to list on NSE. NSE and Jio represent two important pillars of India's growth story. .Jio IPO listing today: Jio Platforms to debut on Dalal Street shortly .Reliance Jio listing: Jio Platforms shares indicate 21.36% premium in NSE pre-open session Jio Platforms shares were trading at Rs 1,358 in the NSE pre-open session, marking a premium of Rs 239, or 21.36%, over the issue price. The pre-open indication pointed to a substantial premium over the IPO issue price, as investors tracked the listing of the telecom and digital services company. The NSE data listed the security as Jio Platforms Limited, with the identifier INE0BJO01010..JIO IPO listing: When will Jio Platforms shares start trading on NSE and BSE? Jio Platforms is set to make its debut on the NSE and BSE at 10 am. Ahead of regular trading, the shares are expected to go through a special pre-open session, as prescribed under the standard equity-market listing process..JIO IPO listing: 22% GMP hints at a strong listing premium Jio Platforms’ IPO grey market premium (GMP) stood at Rs 248, indicating a premium of 22.2%. The mainboard issue had a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share, with a total issue size of Rs 30,187.65 crore. The grey market premium is an unofficial indicator and does not guarantee the price at which shares will list on the stock exchanges..Reliance JIO IPO listing: Jio Platforms eyes growth through AI, cloud computing and 6G technology Jio Platforms is looking to expand beyond telecom, with technology, artificial intelligence and cloud computing expected to drive its next phase of growth, the telecom giant's managing director Akash Ambani told PTI earlier. “There is no either-or at Jio: the network is our technology,” Ambani said, highlighting the company’s in-house 5G core, cloud-native radio access network and software platform, which serves 533.3 million customers. The company is also exploring satellite connectivity and next-generation 6G technology as areas for future development. Ambani said Jio’s growth opportunities span mobile services, home broadband and digital solutions for enterprises. He pointed to the scope for expansion, noting that around 26 crore Indians still use 2G services, while fixed broadband reaches only about 21% of households in the country..JIO IPO listing: QIB portion subscribed 70.55 times Qualified institutional buyers led the demand for Jio Platforms’ initial public offering, subscribing to their reserved portion 70.55 times. The non-institutional investor category was subscribed 14 times, while the retail investor portion was subscribed 2.72 times. The portions reserved for employees and Reliance Industries shareholders were subscribed around 2.93 times and 7.6 times, respectively. Overall, the IPO closed with subscriptions of 22.19 times the shares on offer. The category-wise figures show the level of demand across institutional, non-institutional, retail, employee and shareholder segments during the issue’s three-day subscription window..Jio IPO Listing: Mukesh Ambani’s plan to build an ‘everything company’ The listing of Jio Platforms furthers Mukesh Ambani’s plan to transform Reliance Industries from an oil-and-chemicals conglomerate into an “everything company” spanning consumer and technology businesses. Jio Platforms is Reliance Industries’ telecom and digital services unit and serves more than 530 million customers. Its initial public offering raised $3.2 billion and valued the company at up to $108.3 billion. The listing ceremony is expected to be attended by Akash Ambani, Mukesh Ambani’s eldest son and Jio Platforms’ managing director, according to an industry source with direct knowledge. The company’s stock market debut is scheduled for Wednesday, October 28..Reliance Jio IPO: Reliance shares deliver around 900% returns in two decades Over the last two decades, Reliance shares have delivered returns of around 900%, outperforming the benchmark Nifty index’s 685% return over the same period, according to LSEG data. Jio Platforms, the company’s telecom and digital services unit, is now set to make its stock market debut following its $3.2 billion IPO. The issue attracted strong demand, closing with subscriptions of 22.19 times the shares on offer. Jio Platforms is valued at up to $108.3 billion ahead of its listing on Wednesday, October 28..Reliance Jio IPO: Investor demand build rapidly from day 1 Jio Platforms’ IPO was fully subscribed within the first 100 minutes of opening on October 21. The rapid response continued over the three-day bidding period, with the issue subscribed more than five times by Day 2 before closing at 22.19 times on October 23. In most Indian IPOs, subscription levels typically build gradually, with institutional investors often placing bids closer to the deadline. Jio Platforms’ offering saw substantial demand from the beginning of the subscription period. The issue was priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share, with a lot size of 12 shares..JIO IPO listing: India ranks first by IPO deal count this year India has become the world’s busiest initial public offering market this year by the number of deals, with 246 listings so far. However, it ranks fourth by the amount of money raised, at $13.5 billion, behind the United States, mainland China and Hong Kong, according to LSEG data. Jio Platforms’ $3.2 billion offering is India’s largest IPO and attracted bids worth $77 billion. The listing is being closely watched as a test of investor appetite for large public offerings amid increased scrutiny of artificial intelligence-linked stocks. Several brokerages have described Jio Platforms’ $108.3 billion valuation as attractive, while flagging competition, heavy capital spending and changes in telecom rules as risks. .Reliance Jio IPO: ADIA, BlackRock and Fidelity among investors Jio Platforms’ initial public offering received substantial demand from anchor investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity. The $854 million worth of shares reserved for these investors received bids exceeding $25 billion on Monday, according to the provided inputs. The anchor investor response preceded the three-day public subscription period, during which the issue attracted around 1.3 crore applications. The $3.2 billion IPO was fully subscribed within its first 100 minutes and closed with overall subscriptions of 22.19 times. Total demand, including the anchor investor portion, approached Rs 7.5 lakh crore, according to reports..Jio IPO Listing: GMP indicates blockbuster 22% premium Ahead of Jio Platforms’ stock market debut, the grey-market premium indicated potential listing gains of about 22%. The grey market is an unregulated market in which investors trade in shares before they are listed on the stock exchanges. The premium is an indication of the price at which unlisted shares are being traded relative to the IPO price. Jio Platforms’ issue was priced between Rs 1,065 and Rs 1,119 per share, with the upper end of the price band at Rs 1,119. However, the grey-market premium does not establish the actual listing price. The company’s market debut on Wednesday will determine its listing price..Reliance Jio IPO: Jio IPO attracts around 1.3 crore applications Jio Platforms’ initial public offering became the first public issue globally to receive more than one crore applications. The issue attracted around 1.3 crore applications, according to reports, as demand surged during the three-day bidding period. The $3.2 billion offering drew interest from institutional and retail investors, employees and shareholders. Subscription levels rose sharply after the IPO opened on October 21 and closed on October 23. The issue was subscribed 22.19 times overall, while total demand, including the anchor investor portion, approached Rs 7.5 lakh crore, according to reports..Jio IPO listing: Jio Platforms set for stock market debut Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital services unit of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries, is set to list on the stock exchanges on October 28. The company’s $3.2 billion initial public offering has become India’s largest public issue, attracting strong interest from institutional and retail investors, employees and Reliance Industries shareholders. Jio Platforms is valued at up to $108.3 billion, potentially making it one of India’s biggest companies by market capitalisation when trading begins. The listing follows a three-day subscription period from October 21 to October 23, during which the issue was subscribed 22.19 times overall.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Following up on GST Council decisions, Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs has issued over half a dozen detailed circulars on steps to reduce litigation and appeals, issuing show cause notices to taxpayers and speeding up registrations and changes that businesses need to make. In addition, it has sought to address concerns around exports as well as sectoral issues such as those related to banks and NBFCs.Tax authorities have underlined the need to facilitate registration while ensuring that there is no misuse. “While there is a need to exercise due diligence in processing registration application to prevent GST registration form being obtained by unscrupulous and fraudulent elements for passing on input tax credit (ITC) without any underlying supply, at the same time, it is also important to ensure that genuine applicants seeking registration are able to complete the process without undue inconvenience,” CBIC said in the circular, while pointing to grievances that it had received due to difficulties faced by taxpayers.It specifies that pre-show cause notice intimation may be given to taxpayers, wherever feasible, so that they can clarify their position prior to the start of formal proceedings.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Oil prices edged higher again on Wednesday, with Brent crude crossing $115 a barrel after declining in previous sessions.
articles.body: Oil prices edged higher again on Wednesday, with Brent crude crossing $115 a barrel after declining in previous sessions. The rebound came after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery, reviving concerns over oil supplies from the Middle East amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran and its proxies.Brent crude gained $1.22, or 1.07%, to trade at $115.10, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $0.96, or 0.96%, to $100.90.The Houthis on Tuesday said that they targeted the refinery, which has a processing capacity of 550,000 barrels per day. The claimed strike marked an escalation in their attacks against Saudi Arabia, the world's second-largest crude producer. Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the attack.The latest gains followed a decline of nearly $2 in oil prices on Tuesday, when talks in the Middle East helped ease concerns over supply disruptions. The reported strike brought those concerns back into focus.Expectations of higher crude inventories in the US provided another factor for the oil market to consider. US crude stockpiles increased by around 15,000 barrels in the week ended October 23, according to a Reuters poll of eight analysts.On the production front, OPEC+ members are expected to maintain their December oil output targets at Sunday's meeting, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. The expected decision is in line with market expectations.Output in most of the group's seven core members, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman, is already below their respective production targets.Meanwhile, Russia's crude oil shipments from its Baltic and Black Sea ports could decrease next month, traders said.The potential decline comes as Russian domestic refiners prepare to increase diesel production following a deal with Washington this month.Oil prices have remained volatile as the Middle East crisis enters its eighth month. articles.title: Mukesh Ambani gets teary-eyed as Anant, Akash, Isha talk about Reliance's journey at Jio listing
articles.summary: Jio share listing: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani got emotional at Jio Platforms Limited’s listing ceremony as he watched his children speak
articles.body: Jio share listing: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani got emotional at Jio Platforms Limited’s listing ceremony as he watched his children speak about the family’s legacy and Jio’s journey. Sitting beside his wife, Nita Ambani, the 69-year-old chairman listened as Isha, Akash and Anant Ambani addressed the gathering ahead of the NSE bell-ringing ceremony.The occasion was particularly significant for Reliance, marking its first listing in two decades with the stock market debut of Jio Platforms Limited. The ceremony brought together the company’s history, the contribution of its founders and the responsibility its next generation now carries.Jio Platforms made a strong debut on Dalal Street, listing at Rs 1,359 on the BSE and NSE, a premium of 21.36% over its IPO issue price of Rs 1,119 per share. The Rs 30,213-crore public issue was subscribed 22.19 times, making it India's largest IPO to date and valuing the Reliance Industries-backed digital services business at over Rs 10 lakh crore.Isha Ambani recalls father's early days at RelianceIsha Ambani, executive director of Reliance Retail Ventures, took the gathering back to the company's beginnings, recalling a recent family dinner during which her father spoke about Reliance's first public offering in 1977. Mukesh Ambani was 20 at the time, while his father, Dhirubhai Ambani, had decided to take the company to the public."A few evenings ago, at our dinner table, my father, Shri Mukesh Ambani, was remembering his days in 1977. He was 20 years old, working on Reliance's first public offering. My grandfather, Shri Dhirubhai Ambani, had decided to take Reliance to the people," she said.Isha also recalled the maxim associated with her grandfather, 'Growth is life', and vowed to continue building the business and creating value for shareholders. She said Akash had worked hard for 13 years to build and grow Jio into India's largest telecom company, with over 53 crore subscribers.Isha planted Jio's idea, says brother AnantAnant Ambani, executive director of Reliance Industries, recalled how Jio grew from an idea planted by his sister Isha and nurtured by her twin brother, Akash. Reflecting on Reliance’s journey and its global ambitions, he said, “Once-barren land of Jamnagar turned into the site of the world's largest refinery. He showed the world that when India builds, the world takes notice. Then came the New India, the young India, and a new dream: internet in every hand and the world within reach of every village. The name of that dream was Jio. The seed of this dream was planted by Isha Didi, and Akash Bhai made that seed his own dream. Jio was then taken to every corner of the country.”The ceremony also highlighted the scale of investor interest in the company. Akash said that the IPO received demand worth Rs 7.5 lakh crore through 1.3 crore applications, with the issue fully subscribed within 95 minutes of its launch. He described the response as deeply humbling and said it had left him with a profound sense of responsibility.The entire Ambani family, including the next generation, rang the bell as the clock struck 10 am. By 11.01 am, Jio Platforms shares were trading 21.42% higher at Rs 1,358.7 on the BSE, against a 0.89% decline in the benchmark index.Akash Ambani calls listing a ‘start line’Jio Platforms managing director Akash Ambani said the listing was not a finish line but a start line. He promised to take the company to greater heights and grow investor wealth, as Reliance Industries has done over nearly 50 years."We promise to take Jio to greater heights of growth, excellence and reputation in India and the world," the 35-year-old said at the NSE ceremony, attended by his parents, siblings and grandmother Kokilaben.Akash said the next generation's responsibility was not simply to preserve what it had inherited, but to make Jio bigger, better and more meaningful for India.He said Jio had democratised data in its first decade and would now focus on making more technologies accessible."In our next ten (years), we want to democratise every technology that can transform Indian lives: AI, cloud, connected devices, connectivity even from space and digital services not yet imagined," he said.Akash described the company's ambition as building a digital society where connectivity, computing and intelligence work together seamlessly. He said India was emerging as a creator of technology rather than merely a consumer. "We are now ready to take the tricolour global", he added.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Jio marks historic NSE debut after breaking India's IPO records in just 95 minutes
articles.summary: Marking a watershed moment for Indian capital markets, Reliance Industries' digital and telecommunications arm, Jio Platforms Limited, made a blockbuster
articles.body: Marking a watershed moment for Indian capital markets, Reliance Industries' digital and telecommunications arm, Jio Platforms Limited, made a blockbuster debut on the National Stock Exchange on 28 October. In a grand ceremony that showcased a generational shift, the entire Ambani family, led by Mukesh and Nita Ambani, alongside the third generation of leaders, rang the ceremonial bell to officially list the technology giant.The stock debuted at Rs 1,358 to Rs 1,360 on the NSE, reflecting strong investor confidence as the benchmark Nifty50 traded near 22,591. The listing follows a historic initial public offering that shattered domestic records.Record-breaking demandAddressing the gathering, Akash Ambani revealed the unprecedented scale of the public issue. He announced that India's largest IPO was fully subscribed within just 95 minutes of its launch, making it the fastest in the country's history."We garnered over Rs 7.5 lakh crore of demand, the highest ever India has seen," Akash Ambani said. "And over 1.3 crore Indians trusted us with their wealth, the highest ever application count India has seen."He noted that when the project began, the company had zero revenue and zero customers. Today, the platform serves over 540 million users."My dream is that one day, when the world counts its great technology companies, one of them will be from India, and that company will be called Jio Platforms Limited," he added.Legacy and social impactThe ceremony heavily emphasised the theme "Thank you, India. Jio aapne banaya." Isha Ambani drew a historical parallel to the year 1977, when a 20-year-old Mukesh Ambani assisted founder Dhirubhai Ambani in taking Reliance public. That issue raised Rs 2.82 crore at a Rs 10 crore valuation from ordinary citizens."Almost 50 years later, that trust has come full circle," Isha Ambani said. She highlighted the company's financial strength, noting that this year Jio earned about USD 15.5 billion in revenue and USD 8 billion in real earnings.Anant Ambani anchored his speech on the social and emotional impact of digital connectivity, dedicating the milestone to the 53 crore members of the Jio family."Today, the bell at the Exchange will ring for me like a temple bell," Anant Ambani said. "Because for me, business is Puja. And every Puja ends with Prasad. Prasad is always shared. Today, Jio is shared with India."He highlighted how the network empowered rural citizens, students, and soldiers, serving as the invisible backbone for India's digital aspirations. articles.body: New Delhi: Record vehicle sales could not shield Maruti Suzuki from a sharp fall in quarterly profit as higher costs and investment losses squeezed earnings. India's largest carmaker reported standalone net profit of Rs 2,415 crore for July-Sept, down 27% year-on-year. Net sales rose 26% to a record Rs 50,616 crore, while vehicle sales increased 26.5% to an all-time quarterly high of over 6.9 lakh units.The earnings decline came as commodity inflation linked to West Asia disruptions pushed up costs. Total expenditure rose nearly 30% to Rs 50,604 crore, outpacing sales growth.Raw material and component expenditure increased 48% to Rs 37,488 crore amid higher production volumes and cost pressures. Operating profit fell 17% to Rs 2,804 crore from Rs 3,382 crore a year earlier.Mark-to-market losses on invested surplus added to the pressure, pulling non-operating income down to Rs 430 crore from Rs 966 crore.Demand remained strong, with small-car sales rising 35.9% and utility vehicle volumes growing 68.2%.Exports, however, declined to 1.08 lakh vehicles from 1.1 lakh vehicles in the corresponding quarter last year.Standalone revenue from operations, including servicing and ancillary income, increased to Rs 53,340 crore from Rs 42,332 crore. Consolidated net profit fell 26% to Rs 2,466 crore, while consolidated revenue reached Rs 53,356 crore. articles.title: Nifty 50 heads for worst year in a decade: Should you buy stocks now or wait?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Dalal Street is having a rough ride in 2026, with the Nifty50 falling 13% this year.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Dalal Street is having a rough ride in 2026, with the Nifty50 falling 13% this year. The fall may tempt investors to buy stocks at lower prices, but is it the right time to jump in?According to Thyagesh Baba, non-executive director at Spark Capital Advisors, slowing economic growth, elevated crude oil prices and stretched valuations could continue to cap market returns.The Nifty50 is heading for its worst annual performance in more than a decade, following a near threefold rise over the past 10 years. For investors eyeing the market dip as a buying opportunity, the big question is whether companies can sustain earnings growth and whether an improvement in market conditions can pave the way for stronger returns.Speaking to Reuters on Tuesday, Baba said that the index’s outlook for next year would hinge on sustained earnings growth, foreign investors returning after record outflows, easing crude prices and a revival in private investment.Though he did not give a specific target for the market, the expert indicated that investors should pay closer attention to companies’ ability to deliver earnings growth than expect widespread gains from higher valuations.Is it time to buy?The stock market’s weak performance alone may not be a sufficient reason to buy, given the challenges that remain. Slowing growth, high oil prices and stretched valuations could limit the scope for returns even after the correction.Earnings performance could offer investors a more useful indicator. Nifty 50 companies are expected to report 20% profit growth in the September quarter, their fastest pace in three years. However, Baba said investors who had grown accustomed to annual earnings growth of 20%-25% should recognise that even 16% growth would be robust in an economy recording nominal growth of 10%-12%.This puts the focus on whether companies can deliver sustainable profits rather than on expectations of a broad-based rise in stock valuations.What could support the market?A return of foreign investors could be an important factor in the market’s outlook, particularly after record outflows. A moderation in crude oil prices and a revival in private investment are also among the conditions Baba identified as relevant to the Nifty’s performance next year.He also pointed to improvements in India’s banking system and corporate balance sheets. Years of regulatory tightening have left the banking system healthier, while companies have reduced leverage and become more disciplined in allocating capital."The old model of borrowing at 18%-20% to fund businesses generating 11%-12% returns on capital has largely faded," he said.These improvements provide a positive aspect to the outlook, although Baba’s assessment of future market returns remains tied to earnings delivery and the broader investment environment.The 13% decline in the Nifty50 does not, by itself, establish whether the market is ready for a sustained recovery. According to Baba, future returns are likely to depend more on companies delivering earnings growth than on broad-based valuation gains.Therefore, investors looking to buy after the market fall should watch whether companies can sustain their earnings, foreign investors return, crude oil prices fall and private investment picks up. These factors will shape the market’s performance next year, while slower economic growth and high stock valuations could limit returns.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. articles.title: Israel’s stock market drops as exit polls show no clear election winner
articles.summary: Benchmark Tel Aviv 125 index falls more than 3 percent amid uncertainty over who will lead the next government.
articles.body:
Israel’s stock market has fallen sharply amid exit polls showing no clear winner in the country’s parliamentary elections.

The benchmark Tel Aviv 125 index dropped as much as 3.5 percent in early trading on Wednesday as investors weighed the unclear results of Israel’s first election since the start of its genocidal war on Gaza.

Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition nor the opposition bloc headed by Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot appeared on track to gain a parliamentary majority in the 26th Knesset.

With more than 84 percent of votes counted as of 11 GMT, Netanyahu’s coalition was on course to win 54 seats, while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc was headed for 49 seats, according to tallies published by Israeli media.

Sixty-one seats are needed to form a majority in the unicameral parliament.

Israel’s economy has been running hot despite being on a war footing for the past three years amid an influx of investment in the local tech sector.

Gross domestic product (GDP) grew 2.9 percent in 2025 and 3.2 percent in the first half of 2026, according to government figures.

The Bank of Israel last week raised its GDP growth forecast for all of 2026 to 5.6 percent, up from 4 percent, citing ramped-up production by Israeli firms overseas.

The central bank has forecast that GDP growth for 2027 would reach 7.5 percent, far surpassing estimates for advanced economies such as the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany and Japan.

articles.title: Fed likely to hold rates steady ahead of midterms
articles.summary: Federal Reserve officials will decide whether to raise interest rates again on Wednesday, as persistent inflation strains Americans ahead of the midterm elections. Annual inflation was 3.7 percent in September, according to the consumer price index (CPI). That marked an increase from 3.4 percent in August and showed inflation remains entrenched in the economy amid…
articles.body:
Federal Reserve officials will decide whether to raise interest rates again on Wednesday, as persistent inflation strains Americans ahead of the midterm elections.

Annual inflation was 3.7 percent in September, according to the consumer price index (CPI). That marked an increase from 3.4 percent in August and showed inflation remains entrenched in the economy amid the ongoing Iran war .

But despite that data, multiple central bank officials — including Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and John Williams, the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York — have recently said they will evaluate economic trends before backing another rate hike.

“They’ve signaled pretty clearly that they’re going to be holding this meeting,” Patrick Harker, the former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, told The Hill.

When the Fed raised rates by a quarter point last month, it marked a bid to contain inflation , which has stubbornly remained at more than 2 percent since the winter of 2021.

After the decision, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was clear that inflation has been “too high” for “too long,” arguing the central bank had to remove a “dose of accommodation” from the economy.

“This summer’s inflation readings do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved,” Warsh told reporters last month.

After the Fed raised rates, 16 of 18 officials on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), excluding Warsh , projected at least one additional rate hike this year.

Hawkish rhetoric from the likes of Fed Vice Chair Michael Barr and Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson followed, as both previewed additional hikes .

“Looking ahead, if conditions evolve as I expect, some modest further tightening may be warranted,” Paulson said at a financial technology conference on Sept. 24.

But officials have emphasized they will keep evaluating economic data before making a decision . After Wednesday, the rate-setting panel will meet again on Dec. 7-8.

Williams said in late September there is “no need for urgency” on the part of the FOMC, while Jefferson said earlier this month policymakers may need “more time” before backing another rate hike.

Markets, which initially anticipated a second straight hike, have flipped the switch in recent weeks.

Traders are pricing in a 92.8 percent chance the central bank will hold rates steady as of Tuesday afternoon, according to the CME FedWatch tool , after forecasting a roughly 64 percent chance of a quarter-point hike a month ago.

“I don’t expect them to move this week,” Dr. Ellen Meade, a former policy and communications adviser to the Fed, told The Hill.

“I’m not expecting them to do anything other than maybe update in the statement their characterization of the economy,” Meade later said.

Hanging over the heads of Fed officials are the midterm elections , with Election Day less than a week away.

President Trump, who has urged the central bank to cut rates , and the GOP face economic headwinds at the ballot box. Democrats, meanwhile, are looking to capitalize on voters’ frustrations with high prices and take back control of Congress.

Meade, now a research professor of economics at Duke University, said Fed officials prefer to hold rates steady close to an election if feasible.

While the central bank raised rates by three-quarters of a point in November 2022, days before the midterms, that was the sixth in a string of 10 consecutive hikes. Inflation rose to a 40-year high of 9.1 percent in June of that year, according to the CPI .

“They’re not in a ‘we need to move every meeting’ [mindset], like they were in 2022,” Meade said of Fed officials.

Heather Long, the chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, similarly told The Hill earlier this month that policymakers will hold rates steady given it is a “coin flip” decision and the election is days away.

But Harker, the former Philadelphia Fed president, argued otherwise. Noting inflation has remained at more than 2 percent for five and a half years, he said the choice Fed officials face on Wednesday is “not much of a toss-up.”

“One shock is bad luck, but three in five years is a pattern. … You see these shocks after shocks coming at you, and you can’t just keep looking through them because they are causing this inflationary behavior we’re seeing,” added Harker, who has taught at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School since leaving the Philadelphia Fed.

Even if policymakers raise rates, monetary policy decisions typically take effect in 12 to 18 months. Higher rates would not immediately impact spending by consumers and businesses, although Meade acknowledged they could affect “sentiment” toward the economy.

“I don’t think raising the fed funds rate is going to make a whole lot of difference in terms of the macro economy,” Harker said.

But elevated borrowing costs are already a troubling sign for Republicans, as the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate is at more than 7.3 percent , an increase of about 1.3 percentage points from the week before the Iran war began, according to data from Freddie Mac.

The average credit card interest rate hit 19.7 percent earlier this month, the first time it had done so since December 2025, Bankrate reported .

Trump, while praising Warsh, has faulted the Fed for higher mortgage rates, even though they were rising — as a result of surging bond yields — before the central bank hiked rates in September.

“You have a board that would like to see the country do badly, in my opinion, because I think interest rates should come down,” the president said earlier this month , when a reporter asked him about high mortgage rates.

Despite Trump blaming his colleagues for higher borrowing costs, Warsh has remained resolute, stating his goal to bring inflation down to 2 percent throughout his five-plus months leading the Fed.

Harker specifically highlighted Warsh’s August speech in Jackson Hole, Wyo., as an example of the first-year Fed chair defining how he “thinks.”

During that speech, Warsh said the “responsibility” for five-plus years of inflation above 2 percent “ sits squarely ” with the Fed. He also left the door open to future rate hikes, saying policymakers would have “work to do” if inflation did not cool off.

Harker praised those remarks, arguing Warsh pivoted after providing a “lack of clarity” about how he would tackle inflation during his first three months in charge. But the former Philadelphia Fed president said Warsh has to “deliver” on that rhetoric.

“Words are cheap. You got to act, and you got to act by actually getting inflation under control,” Harker said.

articles.title: The stock market's best 6 months of the year start Monday: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: The stock market's favorite season starts Monday, with a midterm-year record that hasn't lost since the 1940s.
articles.body:
The stock market's favorite season starts Monday. For decades, November through April has beaten the rest of the year by a mile.

That's the Halloween indicator , also called the "best six months" or "sell in May." Buy stocks at the end of October, hold them through April, then step aside for the summer.

Yale Hirsch found the pattern in 1986. "You can divide the year into two sections and have practically all the gains in one six-month section and very little in the other," his son Jeffrey Hirsch, editor in chief of the Stock Trader's Almanac, wrote in the 2026 edition.

Since 1950, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) has gained an average of about 7% from November through April, versus less than 1% from May through October, according to the Stock Trader's Almanac. Put $10,000 into only the good half each year, and it grew to about $1.3 million. Put it into only the bad half, and it shrank to about $4,300.

This has held up since its discovery. In the 39 years after 1986, the good half turned $10,000 into about $1.2 million, versus about $5,800 for the bad half, by the Stock Trader Almanac's count.

By Yahoo Finance calculations, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained an average of about 7% from November through April between 1950 and 1987, versus about 1% from May through October.

Since 1988, the summer stretch has averaged about 3%. Over the past 10 years, the two halves have been dead even, at about 7% each. May through October came out ahead in five of those years, including a gain of about 23% in 2025.

Hirsch has seen the calendar shift too. "Anticipators, shifts in cultural behavior and faster information flow have altered seasonality in recent years," he wrote.

Index funds and 401(k)s now keep money flowing into stocks every month — one reason "sell in May" has been a bad strategy this century . This year, the S&P 500 is up about 6% since the end of April.

Midterm years are where the good half still shines.

In midterm election years since 1950, October and November have been the S&P 500's two best months, according to the Stock Trader's Almanac. And the November-April stretch after a midterm has risen 19 straight times since 1950, with an average gain of about 15%, by Yahoo Finance calculations. That follows stocks' best stretch of a midterm year , the eight sessions around Election Day.

None of this makes summer safe. May through October hold some of the market's worst stretches, including drops of about 15% in 2001, about 18% in 2002, and about 30% in 2008. The better lesson may be to hedge in May rather than go away.

articles.summary: India has “millions of possibilities” to unlock on its path to becoming a developed nation by 2047.
articles.body: India has “millions of possibilities” to unlock on its path to becoming a developed nation by 2047. Realising this potential will require a sharp increase in research and develop - ment spend, greater investment in emerging technologies and skills, and a stronger focus on inclusive and sustainable growth, govt and industry leaders said at TOI Ideas for India 2026.Ports, shipping and waterways min - ister Sarbananda Sonowal said India’s ambition must extend beyond the scale of its achievements. “Sovereign technol - ogy must give India strategic autonomy; inclusive innovation must ensure that no section of Bharat is left behind; and sustainable development must safe - guard the future of Bharat,” he said.Sonowal highlighted initiatives in the maritime sector, including the devel - opment of the Rs 76,000-crore greenfield Vadhavan Port in Maharashtra, a Rs 70,000-crore package to revitalise ship - building and the maritime sector, and a major push to transport cargo through coastal shipping and inland waterways.“Together, these initiatives will reduce our dependence on foreign transship - ment hubs, improve logistics efficiency, attract investment and create new em - ployment opportunities,” he added.Kirloskar Systems chairperson and MD Geetanjali Kirloskar said India had the opportunity to become a leader in critical technologies while improving living standards for ordinary citizens. Achieving ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047 would require industry to build resilient busi - nesses, strengthen energy security, im - prove product quality and adapt to geo - political uncertainties, she said. Kirloskar stressed the need to signifi - cantly increase R&D spend, noting that India spends around $18 billion annu - ally, equivalent to 0.65% of GDP.Greater investment in innovation and sectors such as semiconductors, AI, clean en - ergy, biotechnology and advanced mate - rials would be essential for global com - petitiveness.“India is not just a market of 1.4 billion people; it is an innovation base of 1.4 billion possibilities,” she said, adding that ‘Viksit Bharat’ should be measured not just by economic size, but also by prosperity, happiness, sus - tainability and inclusive development.South Delhi MP Bansuri Swaraj called for India to become a leader in AI rather than being merely a consumer, highlighting its potential to transform agriculture, education, healthcare, women’s safety and the justice system.Swaraj suggested that AI could help decide certain categories of cases, including cheque-bouncing disputes, matters under the Motor Vehicles Act and rent-control cases — within days rather than months or years, as these are largely adjudicated on documentary evidence.She proposed a guaranteed appeal against AI decisions before a human panel, stressing that AI should have no role in decisions involving per - sonal liberty or incarceration. She also proposed assigning a track - ing ID to every criminal case so that AI could help govt track undertrials who had spent a substan - tial period in custody.“No Indian should be in jail merely because he did not file a bail application,” she said. articles.title: Festive season sales are not always bargains: Avoid these 10 money mistakes
articles.summary: By Adhil Shetty Every festive season, Indian households spend with a sense of optimism.
articles.body: By Adhil ShettyEvery festive season, Indian households spend with a sense of optimism. Dussehra, Dhanteras and Diwali bring celebrations, family gatherings and, for many, the biggest purchases of the year. Spending more at this time is not a problem in itself, but small decisions can add up quickly when offers are everywhere and easy EMIs make almost anything feel affordable. The money choices that matter most are made at three moments, before the first purchase, at the checkout and when the bill arrives.Before the sales beginFestive sales are designed to make every purchase feel like a bargain, and the fear of missing out can lead to buying far more than planned. Set a spending limit before the sales begin and list what is genuinely needed. A budget does not take the joy out of the season, but it ensures that the spending is decided by you rather than by the sale.The festive bonus deserves the same thought. It can feel like extra money to spend freely, but it is simply your hard-earned income paid at a different time. Put aside a portion for the festivities, while redirecting the rest towards clearing expensive dues, topping up an emergency fund or investing for a long-term goal. This way, the bonus adds to the celebrations and strengthens your finances beyond them.At the checkoutOnce the shopping begins, the way a purchase is paid for matters as much as the price. No-cost EMIs spread the cost of big purchases over several months, but they are still a loan, and buyers who pay upfront often receive a discount that EMI buyers do not. For example, a television priced at Rs 19,500 with an upfront discount may cost Rs 22,000 on a no-cost EMI. With a smartphone and a laptop bought the same way, the extra cost could reach around Rs 7,500. Compare the total amount payable, not just the monthly instalment, for a clearer picture of the overall cost.The risk grows when one instalment becomes several. A single EMI rarely appears worrying on its own, but a few running together can strain a monthly budget. Suppose a Rs 15,000 purchase is made on a 3-month pay-later plan, a Rs 45,000 television on a 6-month EMI, and a Rs 20,000 shopping bill is charged to your credit card. That adds up to Rs 80,000 owed, with around Rs 2,500 due in the first month. List every existing repayment before taking on another purchase on EMI, to see how much of your monthly income is already committed.The same care applies to gold, which is synonymous with Dhanteras and Diwali. In the excitement of the occasion, don’t overlook the basics. Buy only from a trusted jeweller, check for the hallmark that confirms purity and insist on a proper bill. Making charges on jewellery are usually not recovered on resale, so buyers treating gold as an investment should factor in that cost.Festive deals also attract fraudsters, who know that shoppers are looking for bargains. Fake sale links, calls claiming to be from a bank, and messages about prizes all aim to create a false sense of urgency. Avoid clicking on unknown or unverified links, and check offers only on the official website or app. Never share an OTP, PIN or card details with anyone, however genuine the request may sound.When the bill arrivesThe real test comes a few weeks later. Clearing only the minimum amount due keeps a card account in good standing, but interest continues to build on the unpaid balance. If only Rs 2,500 is paid on a festive card bill of Rs 50,000, the remaining Rs 47,500 is carried forward. With credit card interest at around 3.5% a month, or more than 40% a year, that works out to roughly Rs 1,650 in a month and over Rs 20,000 if the balance stays unpaid for a year. Pay the bill in full by the due date, as this is the surest safeguard against mounting interest.A high credit limit may seem to offer more room to spend, but using most of it makes repayments harder to manage. Spending Rs 1.2 lakh against a Rs 1.5 lakh limit uses 80% of the available limit, well above the recommended 30% to 40%. High usage and delayed repayments can, in turn, weaken your credit score and make future borrowing costlier. Even a 1% higher interest rate on an Rs 8 lakh, five-year car loan can add roughly Rs 24,000 to the total repayment.Payment dates deserve equal attention during the festive rush. Amid festive preparations, entertaining guests and shopping, a credit card bill or an EMI can easily be missed, and the late fee or adverse mark on your credit history can linger long after Diwali. Switch on automatic payments and due-date reminders, which take only a few minutes to set up and can prevent trouble later.Planning for the next yearFestivals come around at the same time every year, yet festive expenses are often managed at the last minute, sometimes on credit. Start a festival fund right after this season. Saving Rs 2,000 a month builds Rs 24,000 in a year and Rs 5,000 a month grows to Rs 60,000, so that next year's celebrations are paid for with savings instead of credit.Most festive money mistakes come from choices made in the moment, often under the pull of an offer. A clear budget, a careful look at existing repayments and a little planning ahead go a long way in keeping the season joyful and the months ahead free of financial stress. Here's to a happy and prosperous festive season for you and your family!(The author is CEO of Bankbazaar.com)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
